business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Procurement of Battery-Grade Lithium Carbonate Powder

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law doctrine historically dominant, with Islamic Sharia applied to personal status and French-influenced commercial and corporate law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Double Taxation Agreements concluded with UAE, Saudi Arabia, China, United Kingdom and other EU/GCC treaty partners

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 (Combating Money Laundering Law), as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 154 of 2019; Executive Regulations of the AML Law as approved by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 1898 of 2019 and subsequent amendments; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; Investor Protection and Companies-Related Amendments under Law No. 4 of 2018; General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Beneficial Ownership and UBO Register filing requirements; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT Rules; Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) rules applicable to non-banking financial sectors where relevant.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each individual shareholder or certified commercial extract of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or foreign corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; documents must be legalized by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate in the country of origin and, where applicable, by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation counsel and registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or Ministry of Justice in the country of signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by Egyptian Embassy/Consulate and Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing, incumbency, or the equivalent corporate status certificate of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign companies registry, chamber of commerce, or licensed corporate agent in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by Egyptian Embassy/Consulate and Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified board resolution (or equivalent corporate approval) authorizing the incorporation of the Egyptian LLC and naming the authorized local signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate secretary, board notary, or legal counsel if notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by Egyptian Embassy/Consulate and Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for the capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank holding the shareholder's operating account in the source jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization if the bank letter requires formal authentication; otherwise accepted as a bank-certified copy under the Egyptian AML KYC standard

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs), directors, authorized signatories, and material counterparties against the following lists and standards: (i) Egypt's national AML/CFT and terrorism financing lists maintained by the Central Bank of Egypt and the Egyptian Financial Supervisory Authority; (ii) the United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List and UNSCR 1267/1988/2231regimes; (iii) the OFAC SDN List and OFAC-sanctioned jurisdictions and sectors; (iv) the European Union consolidated sanctions list; and (v) the Egyptian and international politically exposed person (PEP) databases. Any direct match requires automatic suspension of incorporation, enhanced due diligence, and written approval from GAFI and the designated AML compliance officer before the entity may proceed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI corporate services and Electronic Company Registration System, available through InvestInEgypt.gov.eg and the official GAFI portal at www.gafi.gov.eg, interfacing with the Egyptian Commercial Registry (Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be written in Arabic in the memorandum of association. A Latin-script transliteration may be filed as a trade name or auxiliary name, but the Arabic name is authoritative. The name must not be a mere description of the activity, must be sufficiently distinctive, and must not be confusingly similar to any existing registered name. Foreign corporate names must be transliterated phonetically into Arabic in a manner consistent with the original corporate logo and registration certificate.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Arab (when used in a manner implying government sponsorship)
Islamic (when used in a manner implying religious authority)
Any token or phrase implying affiliation with the Egyptian Armed Forces, public utilities, or a government agency
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant, through the registered Egyptian counsel, must file a written administrative appeal with the GAFI Company Affairs Sector within 15 days from the date of the provisional rejection notice. The appeal must include the original rejection ticket, the proposed alternative names, the Arabic name of the company, and a legal justification based on the Companies Law No. 159 of 1981. GAFI must issue its decision on the appeal within 30 working days. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may proceed with an administrative lawsuit before the State Council (Egyptian Administrative Courts) within 60 days of the final rejection decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or post office box address is not acceptable as the registered office in Egypt. GAFI and the Commercial Registry require a physical Egyptian address. A licensed shared-office or business-center suite used under a valid lease may be accepted, provided the address is capable of receiving service of process, tax notification, and unscheduled government visits. For a wholesale and trading LLC active in customs-cleared shipments, a dedicated commercial address or an industrial/free-zone address is preferred over a residential property.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-High. For a VAT-registered and customs-active trading LLC, the quantified risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is approximately 35% within the first 12 months of first import activity, driven by Egyptian Tax Authority verification campaigns, Commercial Registry substance checks, and GAFI monitoring. The risk increases if the registered office is not genuinely staffed or does not contain appropriate corporate records and original incorporation documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular legalization statutory tariff and prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Arabic Power of Attorney and shareholder identity declarations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary tariff per Egyptian law

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian corporate counsel and licensed notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee for LLC incorporation documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and GAFI fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry registration of the LLC

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the company's memorandum of association in the Egyptian Official Gazette

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Income tax registration and issuance of the tax card
Company seal creation and legalization of corporate books

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office service for the first month (physical address, shared business center), including documented lease evidence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee, including liaison with GAFI, Commercial Registry, and Egyptian Tax Authority

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, particularly Articles 4, 59-73 and 76-89 governing limited liability companies; Executive Regulations issued by Decree No. 96 of 1982, as amended. The Commercial Code and the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 may also apply to registration, foreign investment and commercial operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Companies Establishment and Investor Services Center; subsequent commercial registration is maintained through the Commercial Registry under the Internal Trade Development Authority.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: LLC Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association, submitted through the GAFI unified incorporation application and registered with the Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Egyptian LLCs have no statutory minimum capital requirement under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981. The issued capital must be stated in the incorporation contract and fully paid at incorporation. No statutory escrow account is generally required for an LLC; the banks and GAFI may require evidence of payment or a capital deposit account under current procedural practice. Capital contributions in kind require valuation and supporting evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company subscribe for and issue the quotas stated in the Incorporation Contract, with each quota fully paid in accordance with applicable law. RESOLVED, that the registered office at the address recorded in the Incorporation Contract is adopted as the Company’s registered office, subject to valid lease or ownership evidence. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Manager and authorized to represent the Company before GAFI, the Commercial Registry, Tax Authority, banks, customs, licensing bodies and other governmental authorities. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed compliance and corporate records officer. The Manager is authorized to execute all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the company name and confirm activity eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center or GAFI electronic incorporation platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Arabic and English names, legal form, shareholder details, ownership percentages and intended commercial activities. Obtain preliminary name and activity clearance before executing the incorporation contract. Confirm that trading, importation and storage of lithium carbonate are accurately described and do not imply chemical manufacturing.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of foreign shareholders and managers
National identification cards for Egyptian shareholders and managers
Shareholder powers of attorney, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the GAFI query through the same service channel, amend the activity wording or proposed name, and resubmit. Obtain written clarification where the activity is referred to another licensing authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and authenticate the incorporation contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center; Egyptian Notary Public or competent Egyptian consular authority for powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Arabic incorporation contract and Articles of Association using the GAFI form. Include capital, quota ownership, management powers, registered office, objects, duration, accounting year and liquidation provisions. Foreign corporate documents must be legalized through the issuing country’s competent authorities, authenticated by the Egyptian embassy or consulate, and translated into Arabic by a certified translator in Egypt where required.
required_dossiers: Executed incorporation contract and Articles of Association
Corporate certificates of incorporation and constitutional documents for corporate shareholders
Board or shareholder resolutions approving the investment
Notarized and legalized powers of attorney
Security or sector approvals if requested by GAFI
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure missing legalization, translation, signature, beneficial-owner or address evidence and resubmit the corrected instrument. Replace defective powers of attorney with Egypt-compliant notarized instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center one-stop shop or GAFI electronic incorporation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload or present the incorporation contract, supporting documents and manager declarations. Pay applicable GAFI, notarization, publication, syndicate and registry charges assessed in Egyptian pounds. Obtain the GAFI establishment certificate and the authenticated incorporation documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer the written deficiency notice within the stated period, upload corrected documents, and request escalation to the GAFI company-establishment supervisor if the application remains pending without a recorded reason.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the commercial registration and tax file
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry office through GAFI coordination; Egyptian Tax Authority Tax Office and Tax Registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the GAFI establishment file to obtain the Commercial Registry certificate. Register the company with the Egyptian Tax Authority, obtain the tax registration card, submit the VAT registration application if the company meets the statutory threshold or conducts an activity requiring registration, and register for electronic invoicing where applicable.
required_dossiers: Registered-office lease and proof of date certainty
Bank account or payment details where requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct address, activity, identification or beneficial-owner discrepancies; file an appeal or administrative grievance with the relevant Tax Office or Commercial Registry supervisor if rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the corporate bank account and complete capital records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian licensed commercial bank; Central Bank-regulated banking institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the incorporation contract, Commercial Registry certificate, tax card, manager authorization, beneficial ownership information and specimen signatures. Complete customer due diligence, sanctions screening and enhanced source-of-funds review for foreign shareholders. Deposit subscribed capital or transfer funds in accordance with the incorporation contract and retain bank evidence.
required_dossiers: Board resolution approving the account and signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide enhanced due-diligence documents, amend signatory mandates, or use an alternative licensed bank. Escalate unresolved onboarding issues through the bank’s complaints and compliance channels.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete import, customs and trading registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC), Egyptian Customs Authority and NAFEZA single-window platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the company imports lithium carbonate, register the importer and customs profile as applicable, appoint a customs broker, obtain required import permits or product approvals, and file advance cargo information through NAFEZA. Maintain the supplier SDS, product specification, tariff classification, origin documents, transport classification and end-use records.
required_dossiers: Tax card and Commercial Registry certificate
Bill of lading or airway bill
Import permit or product approval where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tariff, product, consignee or documentation errors through the customs broker and NAFEZA. Obtain a written customs classification ruling or competent-authority referral where the product is treated as regulated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register physical premises and obtain operational clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant local administrative authority, industrial or commercial licensing office, Civil Protection authority and Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before occupying a warehouse, confirm zoning and permitted use, obtain the local operating or premises license, submit fire-protection plans, secure Civil Protection approval, and conduct environmental screening based on the actual storage quantity, packaging, dust controls and waste profile. Do not commence storage until the lease, fire, occupational and environmental conditions are documented.
required_dossiers: Environmental screening or EIA approval, if required
Occupational health and safety risk assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit revised drawings, additional control measures or a corrected environmental classification. Request inspection reattendance and written reasons for refusal; appeal to the competent local authority or EEAA where legally available.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No manufacturing-license board is ordinarily required for a company limited to procurement and wholesale trading. For an industrial establishment or processing activity, the competent authority is the Industrial Development Authority (IDA); for import and product-control matters, GOEIC and the Egyptian Customs Authority may apply.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial trading and import registrations, including the Commercial Registry, Tax Registration Card and applicable GOEIC importer registration; no separate manufacturing operating permit is ordinarily required for pure procurement and wholesale trading. A local premises or warehouse operating license is required where mandated by the relevant governorate or industrial-zone authority.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Activity and site dependent. Pure office-based procurement is generally outside full EIA requirements. A warehouse storing lithium carbonate powder should be screened under the EEAA environmental classification system; Category A, B or C treatment may apply depending on quantities, location, dust generation, waste, fire risk and cumulative impacts. Category C requires a full Environmental Impact Assessment study; the final classification must be confirmed by EEAA or its competent branch before operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with Environmental Law No. 4 of 1994, as amended, and its Executive Regulations. Prevent uncontrolled powder release, provide enclosed handling and suitable ventilation, control particulate emissions, prohibit untreated wastewater discharge, and use licensed contractors for chemical or contaminated waste. Any wastewater discharge, air emission or hazardous-waste classification must meet the applicable EEAA consent, Law No. 4 limits and permit conditions; product SDS and laboratory testing should determine whether the material is hazardous.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain Civil Protection approval for the premises, including fire detection, extinguishing systems, emergency access, signage, evacuation routes, electrical protection and storage separation. Obtain structural-load and electrical-safety inspections where required by the premises authority. Implement Egyptian Labour Law occupational health and safety requirements, chemical SDS access, personal protective equipment, dust control, worker training, incident response, medical surveillance where indicated, and documented inspection of storage racks and handling equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — مصلحة الضرائب المصرية — official e-portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) / Egyptian Foreign Exchange Administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egyptian pound is partially convertible under a managed floating regime. Current account transactions for genuine trade (imports/exports), services, and profit remittances from registered entities are supported by the interbank market when backed by contractual, customs, and tax documentation. Capital account flows such as direct investment, shareholder loans, portfolio investments, and offshore hedging must be pre-approved or notified through CBE's Balance of Payments reporting system; profit repatriation is subject to an annual audited financial statement, tax clearance, and Board approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the CBE's foreign exchange circulars, all export proceeds must be repatriated to Egypt within 90 days from the date of the bill of lading, using an authorized bank. A mandatory surrender ratio of 50% of export proceeds applies unless a sector-specific waiver is obtained; the surrendered portion is converted to EGP at the applicable interbank rate and the balance can be retained in an export FX account and applied toward genuine current account obligations. The CBE may revise the surrender ratio via circulars during emergency foreign exchange conditions.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low direct viability as a primary treasury rail. Offshore digital EMI accounts (Wise, Mercury, Airwallex) cannot receive Egyptian export proceeds or hold EGP onshore, because Egyptian exchange control law requires all export proceeds and shareholder capital injections to enter through an Egyptian authorized bank unless a special CBE approval is obtained for maintaining a foreign account. Offshore EMIs may only be used for incidental pre-financing or documentation payments that are ultimately re-routed to Egypt. A resident LLC opening an offshore EMI account must report it under CBE Law No. 194/2020 and will face enhanced due diligence at every Egyptian counterparty bank due to the unknown flow of foreign funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandated. Egyptian banks require the legal manager or authorized signatories to appear in person for the initial account opening of a foreign-owned LLC; remote onboarding is not available for medium-risk trading entities. The bank will conduct an interview covering the business rationale, source of initial capital, end-buyers, ultimate suppliers, expected volume, and export/import chain. For non-resident UBOs, notarized and apostilled or Egyptian-consulate legalized passport copies and powers of attorney are accepted, but at least one named director or officer of the LLC must be physically present to sign the account mandates and internal AML risk assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed LLC with foreign shareholders and no domestic operational footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial Registry extract; tax card; lease or ownership certificate for the registered office; GAFI incorporation certificate; detailed board resolution explaining purpose and authority; notarised opening balance sheet or audited combined financial statements; UBO biometric/notarised passport copy; source of funds warranty; expected transaction matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade in high-risk commodity (battery-grade lithium carbonate) with no visible physical storage or processing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade documentation set: proforma/commercial invoice, supplier KYC and corporate registration, transport contracts, bill of lading, marine/cargo insurance, warehouse receipts, independent inspection reports (SGS/Ctac/Bureau Veritas), customs declaration, NAFEZA import registration and bank transfer instructions showing shipment mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment to a supplier that is not the same entity named on the Letter of Credit or supplier invoice
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written know-your-supplier policy, sanction/OSINT screening reports on each beneficiary, supplier board resolution and registration certificates, valid sales/purchase agreement with anti-touting clause, full payment trail from downstream customer to upstream supplier, and management undertaking explaining any back-to-back trade settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High reliance on shareholder debt rather than paid-up equity creating a thin-capitalisation concern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal debt-to-equity policy, executed shareholder loan agreement with arm's length commercial interest rate, consolidated financial statements, solvency certificate, CBE capital registration record, tax auditor report, board resolution allocating the funding between equity and shareholder loan, and a cash-flow forecast for debt service.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital injection must be routed from the beneficial owner's account by SWIFT MT103 through correspondent clearing into the LLC's capital escrow account at the licensed Egyptian bank. The remittance must carry the Egypt Balance of Payments purpose code '401 – Direct Investment Equity' for equity contributions or '402 – Direct Investment Loan' for shareholder loans. The receiving bank will require the GAFI-certified incorporation documentation, board resolution authorising the capital increase, source-of-funds warranty executed by the foreign shareholder, sanctioned-entity checks, and the executed escrow account undertaking. Funds are credited only after full verification; any conversion to EGP for local operating expenses is handled at the CBE interbank rate subject to permissible balance limits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For lithium carbonate supplier settlement, the primary clearing rail is a commercial letter of credit opened through an Egyptian authorized bank, either at sight or with a deferred payment tenor up to 90 days, against presentation of commercial invoice, bill of lading, certificate of origin, packing list, quality certificate, and insurance policy. After arrival and customs release, open-account balances and L/C reimbursements are settled via SWIFT MT103 through the Egyptian bank's nostro account. Every outward payment must be matched with a valid import registration form and an approved CBE import ID; foreign exchange release is conditional on verification against the National Single Window (NAFEZA) customs records. Cash-in-advance telegraphic transfers are permitted for low-value urgent spare parts but subject to additional CBE scrutiny.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Authorized bank-provided USD/EGP forward contracts up to 180 days, strictly against confirmed import/export trade documentation and cannot be rolled over without proof of the underlying trade flow.

Institutional offshore NDF contracts for USD/EGP are not accessible to resident Egyptian corporates as a standalone hedge; NDFs may be incorporated only in cross-border shareholder loan agreements through an offshore vehicle with clear treasury justification and CBE approval.

Cross-currency swaps between EGP and USD for debt service on onboarding shareholder loans are permissible after CBE registration, provided the hedging is limited to the principal and interest exposure of the approved loan and does not create open speculative positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 19) covering the fiscal year ended 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Corporate Income Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April of the following fiscal year (4 months after fiscal year-end); 45-day extension available upon reasoned application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing fine from EGP 10,000 (Law 91/2005 Art. 137); late-payment penalty of 2% monthly on unpaid tax; tax card suspension; forced collection proceedings; criminal sanctions for deliberate evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements, members' AGM approval minutes, and profit appropriation resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and Commercial Registry Department, Ministry of Interior
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM required within 6 months of fiscal year-end (by 30 June); certified copies filed with GAFI within 30 days of AGM approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry listing as non-compliant; administrative strike-off after successive defaults; prohibition on profit distribution; fines under Companies Law 159/1981 Art. 154; tax authority may disregard unaudited accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the Tax Card (Bitaqa Darbiyya) and employer registration data update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority - Taxpayer Registration Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January or within 30 days of any change in legal form, registered address, managers, or ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inability to conclude public-sector and government contracts; customs clearance delays; penalty up to EGP 10,000 for operating with an expired or absent tax card

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) confirmation filing and beneficial ownership register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) via the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) electronic platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days of fiscal year-end (by 31 January); within 15 days of any share transfer or change in control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EGP 1,000,000 under AML Law 80/2002 (Exec. Reg. 104/2021); suspension of banking relationships under obliged-entity rules; director criminal liability for false UBO declarations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry annual data verification and renewal of registry certificate status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Department, Ministry of Interior (one-stop shop operated with GAFI for investment-licensed companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On each annual registration anniversary (anniversary rule); all corporate changes filed within 30 days under Law 34/1976
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration fines; prohibition of commercial activity within Egypt; judicial strike-off of the registry record; loss of limited liability for transactions concluded after deregistration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit for all LLCs regardless of size, turnover, or assets (Companies Law 159/1981 Arts. 30-31 and Investment Law 72/2017); at least one certified auditor registered with the FRA must be appointed; no revenue or asset exemption exists
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) - IFRS-converged national standards; full IFRS mandatory for listed companies and licensed financial institutions

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a private UBO register and file an annual UBO confirmation signed by each manager (or the delegated local manager) through the FRA/EMLCU portal; any shareholding transfer changing direct or indirect ownership above 10% or transferring effective control must be reported to the Commercial Registry and ETA within 30 days and reflected in the AGM-approved annual confirmation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free-zone enterprises may qualify for a full corporate income tax exemption up to 50 years under Law 72 of 2017; non-free-zone investment projects may benefit from deductions of 30%–50% of certain capital costs and tax credits for additional labor and equipment expenditures, per ministerial implementing directives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 15 (Bayan 15) – Corporate Income Tax Return, filed electronically via the Egypt Tax Authority e-filing portal (e-Taxes / T2 system)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the close of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, the return must be filed by 30 April and final tax paid by 30 June unless an extended assessment timeline is agreed with the Egyptian Tax Authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from commercial, industrial, professional, and non-resident PE activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Egypt-source income attributable to the Egyptian permanent establishment; unrelated foreign income is excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses, including procurement costs for battery-grade lithium carbonate, handling, and logistics.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include costs actually incurred for the Egyptian PE; expenses must be evidenced by invoices and supporting bank or LC documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation and amortization for fixed assets and intangible assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply statutory Egyptian rates per asset class; only depreciation attributable to PE assets is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate net taxable profit before tax loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute PE profit on a separate-account basis or using an approved revenue-and-expense apportionment formula.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from previous years (maximum five years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply losses only against the same PE's taxable income; loss carryforward is disallowed upon cessation of the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable income after loss offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the net figure subject to the 22.5% headline corporate income tax rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance tax payments and attributable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offset quarterly instalments previously paid against the final assessed CIT liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable with the return or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance of Egyptian CIT after credits must be paid by the statutory final due date; refund claims follow an ETA assessment process.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly delay surcharge of 2% on the unpaid corporate income tax, statutory fines ranging from EGP 1,000 to EGP 20,000 for the return, and possible seizure of the company's bank accounts and goods. Repeated or intentional non-filing may lead to criminal proceedings against the legal representative and an order restricting travel.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced dividend withholding tax rate under an Egypt income tax treaty, the non-resident beneficial owner must (i) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the residence tax authority, (ii) furnish a Form No. 10 treaty relief application to the Egyptian Tax Authority before or at the time of distribution, and (iii) submit a beneficial ownership declaration confirming no conduit arrangement. The payer must withhold at the 10% statutory rate unless the ETA has approved the treaty relief application; over-withheld tax may be reclaimed through the Article 112 refund procedure of Law 91 of 2005.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties – statutory 20%, generally reduced to 10%–15% under relevant DTAs. Interest – statutory 20%, generally reduced to 10%–15% under relevant DTAs. Relief is conditional on the lender/recipient being the beneficial owner, the transaction having genuine commercial substance, and compliance with the treaty-limitation-on-benefits and anti-treaty-shopping rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Ashared Local File must be maintained when the annual aggregate value of connected-party transactions exceeds EGP 10,000,000; a Master File is required when the multinational group entity's consolidated turnover exceeds EGP 200,000,000 (or equivalent in hard currency), in accordance with Ministry of Finance transfer-pricing guidelines and the executive regulations of Law 91 of 2005.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply the Gulf-Cooperation-Council-style ESR as a standalone code, but the Egyptian Tax Authority applies anti-abuse, substance-over-form, and PE-recognition doctrines under Law 91. Free-zone and investment-incentive entities are required to maintain real business premises, adequate staffing, and substantive operational decision-making in Egypt; without actual economic substance, tax exemptions may be revoked and treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of offshore procurement commission income, fabrication of lithium carbonate purchase invoices, or omission of Egypt-source profits in the LLC's corporate tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT reassessment with an 18% annual interest charge, statutory fines of up to EGP 50,000, and imprisonment for up to five years under Law 91 of 2005; Customs violations may add additional penalties if receipts were underpriced for duty evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general managers who knowingly participate in the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall, face asset freezing and travel bans during adjudication, and may be sentenced to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an Egyptian LLC as a letterbox structure with no office, no employees, and no substantive activity solely to access reduced dividend or royalty withholding rates under an Egypt tax treaty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, reclassification of income as Egyptian-source, application of the full 20% or 10% statutory withholding rates, back-assessment of 22.5% CIT on net profit, plus monthly delay surcharges and fines of up to EGP 20,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and shareholders who knowingly organize a sham entity are personally liable for the unpaid taxes and interest; they may also face criminal conspiracy charges and travel bans under Egyptian tax and penal legislation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border lithium carbonate sales to the parent or affiliated trader are intentionally priced below arm's length to shift profit abroad without a functional analysis, benchmarking study, or Local File to substantiate the margin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Egyptian Tax Authority may disregard the pricing, adjust taxable income to arm's length, impose a 30% penalty on the disputed tax amount, and levy a 2% monthly delay surcharge; unsupported invoices are disallowed and cross-border payments treated as dealings with third parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign misleading transfer-pricing documentation are jointly liable for the resulting tax deficiency and penalties; where the arrangement is found to be an intentional sham, they may be subject to personal criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive 'management fees' or artificially structured trademark royalties to the foreign parent as a substitute for dividends, thereby securing deductions and avoiding the 10% dividend withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of the fee or royalty, recharacterization as a deemed dividend subject to 10% withholding, imposition of 20% WHT on any recharacterized interest or royalty, plus late-payment surcharges and fines up to 100% of the unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members who approve fictitious service or licensing agreements are personally liable for the unreported withholding tax and associated penalties; if the arrangement was designed to evade tax, imprisonment is possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Trade-Based Money Laundering / AML Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Procurement and re-export of battery-grade lithium carbonate is structured with inflated or deflated invoices, circular payments, third-party settlement unrelated to the actual exporter, or the use of shell commodity intermediaries without verified counterparty documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egypt's Anti-Money Laundering Law 80 of 2002, intentional trade-based money laundering carries imprisonment of up to 15 years, fines of up to EGP 500,000, and confiscation of laundered assets; the Central Bank of Egypt may also impose enforcement measures on financial institutions handling the funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers have personal liability for failure to file a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) or for enabling the laundering scheme; their personal assets may be frozen, travel banned, and they are subject to criminal imprisonment.
